lead: 110,000 m² and 42 million litres of salt water. The largest aquarium in Europe brings together the world’s most important marine ecosystems, the longest underwater tunnel on the continent and the only family of belugas in Europe.

The Oceanogràfic de Valencia opened on 14 February 2003 and was designed by the architect Félix Candela together with the engineers Alberto Domingo and Carlos Lázaro. With 110,000 m² of surface area, it is the largest aquarium in Europe. It is home to more than 45,000 animals of more than 500 species and reproduces the planet’s main marine ecosystems on two levels: the upper one with outdoor exhibits, and the lower one with the large aquariums and the legendary underwater tunnel.

The water in the complex is pumped directly from La Malvarrosa beach, guaranteeing the quality of the marine habitat. To walk through all the pavilions at a relaxed pace, a whole day is recommended: between 4 and 6 hours of visit, plus the dolphinarium show, included in the ticket.

items.kicker: The largest aquarium in the complex
items.title: Oceans · The underwater tunnel
items.subtitle: 70 m acrylic tunnel · The longest in Europe · Sharks and rays
items.body: The Oceans building is the largest in the Oceanogràfic and one of the largest in the world, with 7 million litres of water. It represents the temperate regions of the Pacific and the Atlantic, connected by the famous 70-metre underwater tunnel: the longest in Europe. Walking through it is the closest thing to diving without getting wet: bull sharks, hammerhead sharks, nurse sharks, mosaic rays and hundreds of fish pass over your head while the blue lights surround you.
facts: 70 m underwater tunnel · The longest in Europe · 7 million litres

items.kicker: The only family of belugas in Europe
items.title: Arctic · The belugas
items.subtitle: Large Arctic igloo · Belugas Plombir, Miranda and Kylu · Walruses
items.body: A large dome in the form of an igloo houses the Arctic area: rocky cliffs and blocks of ice recreate the habitat of walruses and belugas. Belugas — known as “canaries of the sea” for their sophisticated language of whistles and moans — are the undisputed stars of the Oceanogràfic. Plombir, Miranda and their calf Kylu form the only complete family of belugas in Europe. It is a hypnotic space: silence, cold light and the moment when a beluga passes in front of the glass and looks at you.
facts: Only family of belugas in Europe · Includes the calf Kylu · Air-conditioned indoor space

items.kicker: The largest dolphinarium in Europe · Included in the ticket
items.title: Dolphinarium
items.subtitle: Daily bio-educational shows · Bottlenose dolphins · 26 million litres
items.body: The Oceanogràfic dolphinarium is one of the largest in the world: a 26-million-litre pool with stands for more than 1,500 spectators. The bottlenose dolphins star in daily bio-educational shows that combine acrobatics, jumps and games with their keepers, with an environmental awareness focus. The shows are included in the general admission. Several sessions take place each day: check the times on arrival or at reception.
facts: Ticket included · 26 million litres · Several sessions a day · Check times on arrival

items.title: Antarctic · Penguins
items.subtitle: Rocky cliff with nesting and breeding areas
items.body: The Antarctic pavilion recreates a rocky cliff with nesting and breeding areas where a colony of gentoo penguins lives. The facilities faithfully reproduce the temperature and light conditions of the polar environment, allowing you to watch the natural behaviour of these birds in one of the most spectacular settings in the complex. Connected to the Arctic in the polar building, it completes the tour of the extreme-cold ecosystems.
facts: Recreated polar ecosystem · Nesting and breeding area · Polar building next to the Arctic

items.title: Temperate and Tropical
items.subtitle: Tropical fish · Seahorses · Clownfish · Coral reefs
items.body: The Temperate and Tropical building is a large glass dome that represents tropical and subtropical ecosystems: coral reefs, brightly coloured exotic fish, seahorses and reef sharks. The vivid colours of the clownfish, angelfish and parrotfish create a true underwater kaleidoscope. The tour also invites you to travel from the temperate regions of the Pacific and the Atlantic to the warm waters of the Indian Ocean and the Caribbean.
facts: Glass dome · Recreated coral reefs · More than 50 tropical species

items.title: Mediterranean
items.subtitle: The fauna and flora of the sea of Valencia
items.body: The Mediterranean building shows the biological richness of the sea that bathes Valencia through nine aquariums of different formats and nearly 7,400 specimens of fish and invertebrates. A tour of local fauna that includes everything from seahorses and groupers to rock octopuses, lobsters, edible jellyfish and the colourful inhabitants of the Mediterranean seabed. The Oceanogràfic’s water is pumped directly from La Malvarrosa beach.
facts: 9 aquariums · ~7,400 specimens · Water pumped from La Malvarrosa beach

items.title: Islands · Sea lions and seabirds
items.subtitle: South American coasts · Patagonian sea lions
items.body: The Islands habitat is a large outdoor space modelled on the islands along the South American coast, characterised by large colonies of Patagonian sea lions. The complex’s outdoor lakes also house pelicans, flamingos and cormorants, creating a vibrant natural setting visible from the pedestrian walkways around the site. It is one of the most photogenic spaces in the Oceanogràfic on sunny days.
facts: Outdoors · Patagonian sea lions · Outdoor lakes with waterbirds

items.title: Wetlands / Aviary · Jellyfish · Crocodile house
items.subtitle: Mangroves · Luminescent jellyfish · Nile crocodiles
items.body: The Aviary recreates mangroves and wetlands with exotic waterbirds in an outdoor space. The Jellyfish habitat shows the most spectacular species on the planet: luminescent, fried-egg, white-spotted and edible jellyfish, alongside anemones and other seabed invertebrates. The Crocodile house is a large outdoor space with a nesting area for Nile crocodiles. Note: the Aviary usually closes a little earlier for maintenance.
facts: Three habitats in one · Aviary closes earlier · Jellyfish unique in Europe

items.title: Backstage Tour
items.body: Access technical areas: quarantine area, fish kitchen, filtering system. You can even walk over the shark tunnel from above.

items.title: The Sea in Your Hands
items.body: Sensory activity with direct contact with Mediterranean species: sea urchins, starfish and a visit to the ARCA del Mar.

items.title: Living Lake
items.body: A walk through the Albufera ecosystem, watching waterbirds and fish endemic to the Valencian wetlands.

items.title: Classic guided visit
items.body: A 90-minute tour of the most iconic spaces: Oceans, Arctic, Antarctic and the Dolphinarium. Suitable and accessible for all ages.

items.title: ARCA del Mar
items.body: A guided tour of the Marine Animal Recovery and Conservation Area: learn how sea turtles are cared for and rehabilitated.

items.title: Submarine Restaurant
items.body: Dinner or lunch with direct views of the great central aquarium. One of the most unique dining experiences in Valencia.

blocks.title: Tips for making the most of your visit
items: Arrive at 10:00 when it opens: the shark tunnel and the Arctic without crowds are impressive
Start with the indoor habitats (Oceans, Arctic, Mediterranean) and leave the outdoor ones for the afternoon
The dolphinarium is included in the ticket: check the session times on arrival, they are not fixed
Buy your ticket online in advance: you avoid queues and there are discounts on the box-office price
In summer the complex is open until midnight, but the indoor aquariums close at 20:00
The Submarine Restaurant requires compulsory booking days in advance · It is not included in the ticket
